scene: A flat cartoon head with blonde hair, two black dot eyes, thin flat brows and red lips fills the right two thirds of the frame; one hand pinches a tiny glass vial of red liquid beside the right eye. A white-on-red label reading FAKE sits at the left and a thick red arrow curves from its underside along the bottom of the frame up to the vial, with black shapes at the bottom edge under the chin.
mechanism: A single accusation word is wired by an arrow to a small vial of blood, so the viewer is told what to doubt before any context is given.
composition: The head is cropped by the right and top edges and takes roughly 65 percent of the frame, with the FAKE bar on the left and the vial at the exact centre of the arrow loop. The long red arc forces a left-to-right-to-up path from label to vial, and the grey backdrop leaves nothing else competing.
typography: One word in heavy white capitals on a solid red rectangle, about a quarter of the frame wide, so it reads at any size. The title names the Theranos scandal while the thumbnail never names the company, so FAKE adds the verdict the title withholds.
colors: Cool blue-grey backdrop with a pale halo around the head, warm peach skin and yellow hair, and red used three times: the label, the arrow and the vial liquid. Red against the muted grey is the only saturated element, so it separates cleanly.
psychology: Dot eyes, flat brows and a small closed smile give a blank, composed face with no alarm cue. The pinched vial held to the eye adds an inspection pose, and the red label supplies the accusatory signal.
partnership: The title promises a child-simple retelling of a scandal; the image supplies the verdict FAKE and the blood-vial prop, which only reads as a clue if the viewer already links it to the topic. It leaves open what exactly is fake, and does not mention the title's explain-to-a-child angle.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red FAKE bar first, then the red arrow carrying the eye round to the vial, then the blank face behind it.
art: Flat vector cartoon with thick black outlines and a soft glow rim around the head; the vial is small but drawn with the same line weight as the face, so the style is consistent. At 160x90 the vial shrinks to a red speck while the label and the outline of the head stay clear.
strength: One red-boxed word plus a looping arrow tells the viewer where to look and what to suspect in about a second.
weakness: The vial that carries the whole story is only about 5 percent of the frame width, and nothing in the image identifies the company or the case.
bottleneck: Without prior knowledge of the scandal, the blood vial and the word FAKE do not point to any specific topic.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the vial to roughly double its current size and test whether the arrow target reads more clearly at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 24 names no verdict word and relies on a handshake between two uniformed figures, where this frame commits to a single judgement word.

A yellow circle badge with a red rim sits at the lower right of the gut, beside the rectum. The backdrop is a pale blue sky with soft clouds, and no person appears.
mechanism: An anatomical render with pain bolts converging on a hard stool dramatizes the symptom named in the headline, and a before-bed instruction promises a simple fix.
composition: A three-block text stack of yellow, red and green bands occupies the left 55 percent while the colon fills the right 45 percent and reaches the top and bottom edges. The bolts form a radial pattern that pulls the eye to the stool at the centre of the organ, and the text and organ compete at similar size.
typography: Thirteen words in three stacked bands: yellow capitals with a red outline, white on red, and white on green, plus a small badge. Every band is wide enough to read at 160x90, while the badge text becomes a yellow dot. The headline echoes the title's hard-stool and fast-relief claim and adds before bed and clockwork.
colors: Saturated yellow, red and green blocks sit next to salmon-pink gut and a brown stool against a pale blue sky. Red is used for the bolts, the glow and the middle text bar to signal pain and urgency, and the many hues leave no single dominant palette.
psychology: With no face, the emotion comes from the red bolts striking the stool and the question aimed at the viewer. The picture leans on discomfort and relief cues rather than on any person's expression.
partnership: The title says one simple fix ends hard stools fast; the image repeats this as 1 SIMPLE DRINK and adds a timing (before bed) and an outcome phrase (poop like clockwork). The drink itself is never shown, so what to drink stays unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow CONSTIPATED headline first, then the stool in the middle of the red bolts, then the red and green bands down the left.
art: A glossy 3D organ with consistent soft lighting and a visible texture on the stool; the bolts are flat graphics laid over the render, which makes two rendering styles. The sky backdrop is simple, but four text colours and the badge make the frame busy at small size.
strength: The headline stack names the condition, the timing and the outcome in three clear bands that all stay legible at phone size.
weakness: Text, bolts, badge and organ all compete at similar visual weight, so no single element dominates once the frame is small.
bottleneck: Five bold colour blocks fight for first read, and the 1 SIMPLE DRINK badge shrinks to an unreadable yellow dot at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: drop the third green band and keep two text bands to test whether the stool and bolts read as one focal point.
mechanism_secondary: anatomical symptom render with outcome phrase
counterexample: Seq 3 uses a white field with two words and one figure, where this frame stacks four colour bands over a detailed organ.
hero_object: 3D intestine with stool and red bolts
medical_notes: Title and thumbnail promise a fast single-drink fix and show a stool with stone-like lumps and pain bolts in the colon, which dramatizes the symptom beyond what an unnamed drink can support.

psychology: The side glance with a half-smile and a hand on the hip read as relaxed or evasive rather than alarmed. The tension comes from the red glow on the wallet and the large green pile beside it.

colors: A grey-blue sky, grey and white mountain, and a bright orange jacket with a red bag and yellow duffel as the saturated accent. The yellow text is the only element that matches the duffel, and the red dotted route adds a thin accent line.

partnership: The title asks how wolves became dogs; the thumbnail shows one animal seeing the other in a cracked mirror and asks WOLF SWITCH?. It leaves open what the switch is and how it happened, which fits the how-question in the title.

weakness: The word switch is ambiguous, and the thumbnail does not signal time or process, which the title's how-did question implies.

text: SKIN TIGHTENS / EVEN AT 80! / WHEN YOU / ADD THIS!

psychology: A downcast glance at the glass and a small closed smile read as calm focus. The exclamation marks and red box carry the urgency instead of her expression.
partnership: The title promises that adding something to water will firm skin, cut wrinkles and boost collagen for people over 60; the thumbnail raises the age to 80 and shows the action, but never shows what is added. scene: An isometric 3D-rendered barracks room in white-washed wood holds bunk beds, lockers and a small table with a wine bottle. A prisoner in a red-and-pink striped uniform and cap stands at the back and aims a pistol at five soldiers in green uniforms and helmets, who lie or slump against lockers, over the table and across the floor. Small white cups lie around. A yellow PRISONER label points at the prisoner and a black-and-white NAZI label points at the floor figure.
mechanism: A reversed power scene, one armed prisoner standing over five fallen soldiers, shows the outcome that the title's escape-with-an-army claim implies.
composition: The room is drawn from a high angle, with the prisoner upper right of centre, the table at the centre and soldiers placed around it in a ring. The two labels sit at the top left and bottom centre, and the pale white-grey floor gives the red stripes and green uniforms most of the contrast.
typography: Two single words, each in a bold label with a speech-bubble tail: PRISONER in black on a yellow bar and NAZI in black on white. Both are readable at 160x90, and the labels add the roles that the title does not state.
colors: A desaturated white and pale lavender-grey room, with green army uniforms and a pink-red striped prisoner suit as the main colour, and a yellow label as the one bright note. The red stripes are the only warm area, and they separate the standing figure from the pale walls.
psychology: All faces are small, and the information comes from poses: one upright figure with an extended arm and pistol and five slumped bodies. The cues are about threat and reversal, and no facial expression is legible.
partnership: The title says a man escaped Auschwitz using the army he built inside; the thumbnail shows the end state of a prisoner dominating soldiers in a barracks, which gives a dramatic scene but not the how. It reveals a violent outcome that the title leaves open, which carries a medium spoiler risk.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow PRISONER label first, then the red-striped figure with the pistol, then the NAZI label and the fallen soldiers around the table.
art: Clean isometric 3D render with consistent soft shadows and uniform lighting; the characters are small relative to the room. The scene is pale and uncluttered, but at 160x90 the soldiers merge into green shapes and the pistol is invisible.
strength: Role labels on a ring of fallen figures around one standing figure make the power reversal readable within a second.
weakness: The people are only about 10 to 15 percent of the frame height each, so expressions and the pistol are lost at small size.
bottleneck: The pale low-contrast room leaves only the labels and the red stripes carrying the hierarchy at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: crop in on the prisoner and the nearest two soldiers to test whether a closer scene reads more strongly at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 24 puts two large figures face to face with one handshake, where this frame spreads six small figures across an isometric room.

text: YOUR LIFE / IN EVERY DEA RANK [cap: DEA; vest patch: DEA TRAINEE]

He holds a compact submachine gun across his chest. At the right, YOUR LIFE sits in white capitals on a red rectangle above a thinner black line, on a plain white background.
mechanism: A costumed trainee figure with armour and a gun stands for the first rung of a rank ladder, and the headline invites the viewer to picture themselves in each role.
composition: The figure fills the left 35 percent at near full height, with the text block centred on the right 55 percent. The red box is the largest block, and the figure's gun points toward lower right, while white space separates the two halves cleanly.
typography: Six words over two lines: white YOUR LIFE on a red box and a smaller black IN EVERY DEA RANK beneath it. The red line is readable at 160x90, and the black line is thinner but also readable. The words follow the title almost exactly, minus POV and as.
colors: Pure white ground, a red label as the loudest colour, and navy, black and olive-brown on the figure. The navy outfit and red box are the only saturated blocks, and the two sides are separated by white space.
psychology: Slanted black brows, a frown and a stubbled jaw read as a stern, serious stare. The gun held across the chest adds a threat cue, and the badge and vest add authority.
partnership: The title promises a POV walk through every DEA rank; the thumbnail repeats that wording and shows only the trainee level. It adds the first step of the ladder but no hint of the later ranks, so the every rank progression is not visible.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red YOUR LIFE box first, then the scowling face under the DEA cap, then the DEA TRAINEE vest patch and gun.
art: Clean cartoon with a white round head and a detailed tactical vest and weapon rendered more realistically than the head. The mismatch between a blank round face and a realistic gun is deliberate, and the cut-out is clean against white.
strength: A red label with large type and a figure in recognisable agency gear communicate role and topic quickly.
weakness: The headline simply repeats the title wording and the image shows only one rank, so nothing hints at progression.
bottleneck: The DEA TRAINEE patch and badge details turn to small marks at 160x90, so the trainee level is invisible.
action: Hypothesis: add two or three smaller figures at increasing rank behind the trainee to test whether a visible ladder improves the every-rank promise.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses a similar white field with a headline and cartoon figure, but adds a path and goals, where this frame has no progression element.

scene: A giant black SPAIN fills the top 40 percent of the frame. Below it, five cartoon characters stand shoulder to shoulder: a man at the left in a blue suit with a wide-eyed, open-mouthed expression, a dark-haired man in a yellow patterned shirt, a laughing woman with long black hair in a red polka-dot top at the centre, a man with a moustache in a red-and-blue striped football shirt reading Spotify, and a woman at the right with wavy hair in a green top.
mechanism: A single country word over a line-up of five exaggerated characters promises a roll-call of regional types.
composition: The black word spans the full width at the top and the five heads and shoulders run along the bottom, cropped by the bottom edge. The laughing woman in the centre is the largest face, and the faces form a symmetric line that leaves no negative space, so the frame feels densely packed.
typography: One giant word in black heavy capitals, SPAIN, across the top, readable at any size. The title's 17 regions, stereotypes and explained all disappear, so the text adds nothing beyond the country name.
colors: White ground with a black headline, then saturated yellow, red, green and blue clothing across the five characters. The varied hues make a cheerful strip along the bottom, and the black type separates strongly from both the white and the colours.
psychology: The expressions differ across the line: wide eyes and an open mouth at the left, a wide laugh at the centre, a smile under a moustache and steady looks elsewhere. The variety signals comic caricature rather than any single emotion.
partnership: The title promises all 17 Spanish regions and their stereotypes explained; the thumbnail shows one country name and five characters. The count of 17 and the regional split are missing, so the thumbnail looks like a general Spain image.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the giant SPAIN first, then the laughing central woman, then the shocked man at the left and the football shirt at the right.
art: Flat vector cartoon with thick outlines and consistent style across the five characters; the native image is only 360x202, so the outlines are soft and the small Spotify text is barely legible even at native size. At 160x90 the word and the colour strip hold.
strength: A single huge word and a bright strip of characters make the topic and tone clear at any size.
weakness: Only five characters appear and no number or map shows the 17 regions the title promises.
bottleneck: The native file is only 360x202, so there is little room to add finer cues such as region names without losing legibility.
action: Hypothesis: replace two characters with a small numeral 17 and region silhouettes to test whether the regional promise becomes visible.

scene: A cartoon man with spiky dark hair, a raised brow and a sideways glance with a slight smirk fills the left, in a navy polo and pointing his index finger toward the right. In the centre a runner seen from behind, with a green dollar-sign sack on his back, races up a grey perspective path toward two heaps of green money bags and gold coin stacks. At the right edge a red sports car, a gold watch and a palm island each carry a red cross, and a black arrow curves from the headline down toward them.
mechanism: A runner heading for money piles while luxury items are crossed out dramatizes the choice between secret wealth-building and visible spending.
composition: The man's large head fills the left 30 percent, the road narrows to a vanishing point at the top centre, and the crossed-out items stack down the right edge. The perspective path and the pointing finger give strong leading lines, and the headline runs across the full width at the top.
typography: BUILD SECRET WEALTH in heavy black capitals across the top; three words, readable at 160x90. The title's $1,000,000 and most-people-fail framing are not mentioned, so the thumbnail adds the secret angle.
colors: White and light grey ground with black text, a dark navy polo, saturated green sacks and gold coins, and a red car and red crosses as the warm accents. The green money against the red rejected items codes gain against waste.
psychology: A side-eyed glance with one raised brow and a sly half-smile reads as knowing and conspiratorial. The pointing finger and the red crosses push the viewer toward the runner and away from the luxury items.
partnership: The title asks what to do the moment you own $1,000,000 and says most people fail; the thumbnail says to build secret wealth and shows what not to buy. It adds the secret angle but not the million-dollar scenario or the first step.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black BUILD SECRET WEALTH first, then the smirking face, then the runner on the road and the crossed-out car, watch and island.
art: Flat cartoon with clean outlines and consistent perspective on the road; the runner is a different, more realistic drawing than the man. At 160x90 the headline, face and runner survive, while the small crossed-out items become coloured dots.
strength: A runner, a road and crossed-out luxuries make a complete visual story that works next to the headline.
weakness: The smirking man and the road scene compete for attention, and no number or $ amount is shown.
bottleneck: The three crossed-out items on the right are small and packed along the edge, so at 160x90 their red crosses merge into colour dots.
action: Hypothesis: remove the island and watch and keep only the red car with a larger cross to test whether one rejected item reads faster.
mechanism_secondary: path of saving versus crossed-out luxuries
counterexample: Seq 5 shows only a wallet and one pile, where this frame builds a road with goals and rejected items.
expression_label: sideways glance with raised brow and smirk
hero_object: runner with dollar sack on a path

text: NEVER LOSE BALANCE / I'M 70 / DO THIS 5-MIN / EXERCISE
scene: At the right an older man with short white-grey hair and a grey moustache, in navy scrubs with a stethoscope round his neck, points his index finger toward the text with a closed-mouth neutral face against a red gradient. The left is a dark grey panel with I'M 70 in white, DO THIS 5-MIN in yellow and EXERCISE in white. A full-width red banner across the top holds NEVER LOSE BALANCE in white capitals.
mechanism: A first-person age claim, a time limit and an absolute outcome line are stacked over a presenter in medical clothing who points at the instruction.
composition: The red banner spans the top 20 percent, the text column fills the left 60 percent and the man occupies the right 35 percent from his hair to the bottom edge. His pointing finger is a diagonal into the text, and the red wedge behind him is the only part of the frame not covered in text.
typography: Ten words and two numerals over four lines: white NEVER LOSE BALANCE on red, white I'M 70, yellow DO THIS 5-MIN and white EXERCISE. All lines read at 160x90, but the frame is dense. The title's 70+ and exercise are repeated, and the thumbnail adds 5-MIN and a first-person voice.
colors: Red banner and wedge, charcoal panel, and white and yellow type, with navy scrubs and grey hair on the man. Red and yellow are the alarm and attention colours, and the dark grey keeps the type readable.
psychology: A steady direct look, a closed mouth and a gentle point read as a calm instructor, and the stethoscope adds authority. The red banner supplies urgency and the word NEVER supplies an absolute promise.
partnership: The title promises one simple daily exercise for people over 70 to stop falls for good; the thumbnail echoes the age and exercise and adds a 5-minute duration and a never-lose-balance claim. It never shows the exercise, so the content of the instruction stays hidden.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red NEVER LOSE BALANCE banner first, then the yellow DO THIS 5-MIN, then the pointing man on the right.
art: Photorealistic head and scrubs with consistent lighting, and flat colour panels and banners laid over them; the cutout edge is clean against the red wedge. The frame is packed with text, but at 160x90 the banner, the yellow line and the face all hold.
strength: A time-boxed instruction, an age statement and a presenter pointing at the text give the frame a complete pitch.
weakness: The man says I'M 70 while wearing scrubs and a stethoscope, which makes it unclear who is speaking and what their credentials are.
bottleneck: Four stacked text lines plus a banner leave little room for any picture of the exercise, so the text carries the whole promise.
action: Hypothesis: replace the EXERCISE line with a small pose illustration to test whether a visible movement raises the specificity.
counterexample: Seq 11 uses the same red-backed presenter in scrubs but adds a bedside inset, where this frame has only text beside the man.
expression_label: steady gaze with closed mouth, pointing
hero_object: 5-MIN exercise text with pointing doctor-styled man
medical_notes: Scrubs and a stethoscope with an I'M 70 line blur whether the speaker is a clinician, and NEVER LOSE BALANCE is an absolute outcome claim for an unshown exercise.
